h1: SEO Agency in Bangalore: for founders who already know what SEO is
metaTitle: SEO Agency in Bangalore for SaaS and D2C Founders
metaDescription: An SEO agency in Bangalore for SaaS and D2C founders: bottom-funnel keyword maps, organic versus paid CAC in INR, and a 90-day baseline guarantee.
answer: Bangalore SEO is different because most buyers here are product founders who already run paid acquisition. The work that pays is bottom-funnel: alternatives, comparison, integration and pricing pages that catch demand your ads are already buying. Budget ₹40,000–₹75,000 a month, and judge it on cost per qualified lead, not on traffic.
takeaways: Bangalore is where most of India's venture-funded SaaS is headquartered, so the buyer on the other side of the pitch has run keyword research themselves. Skip the education.
The highest-value pages are the ones your sales team already sends in emails: **vs**, **alternatives**, **integrations**, **pricing**.
Kannada barely matters for B2B software search here. For D2C retail and local services it genuinely does — just not in the way most agencies sell it.
Koramangala, HSR and Indiranagar pull each other's local pack. Whitefield and Electronic City do not. Plan store pages accordingly.
On a site under 500 pages, 90 days is a fair window to beat a frozen baseline. On a 50,000-URL marketplace it isn't, and we'll say so before quoting.

sections.h2: The keyword map that matches a Bangalore SaaS funnel
body: Most proposals you'll get in Bangalore open with category head terms and a projected traffic curve. Those take eighteen months and a link budget you haven't approved, while the queries that convert sit unclaimed because they're unglamorous and don't look good in a deck.
Here's the map we build first. Every row is a query your buyer types after they've already decided to spend money.

callout.title: The order matters more than the list
callout.body: Alternatives and comparison pages can rank in weeks because almost nobody writes them well. Category head terms take quarters. Running that order backwards is the commonest reason a Bangalore startup fires an SEO agency in month four.

sections.h2: Organic CAC versus paid CAC, in rupees you can check yourself
body: You already know your paid CAC. Somebody asks about it in every board update, and you can probably quote it to the rupee. So run the organic side through the same arithmetic rather than arguing about sessions.
This isn't a projection and we're not going to pretend we know your conversion rate. It's a method. Put your own numbers in.
numbered: Take your blended paid CAC over the last 90 days. Call it **P**.
Take the retainer. Ours starts at **₹75,000/mo**, or **₹40,000/mo** for smaller sites. Twelve months is ₹9,00,000 or ₹4,80,000, ex-GST.

Divide that by the qualified leads organic produced across the same twelve months. That's your year-one organic CAC — and it will usually look worse than P, because you paid for pages that hadn't started working yet.
Now model year two with the same pages, the same content, and zero new spend on the ones already published. The pages don't stop. **That** is the number worth putting next to P.

callout.title: The asymmetry nobody quantifies for you
callout.body: Paid CAC is honest every single day and never improves on its own — the auction reprices you every quarter. Organic CAC is flattering after year one and useless before month six. That gap is the whole argument for running both, which is why we sell [performance marketing](/performance) next to SEO instead of pretending one replaces the other.

sections.h2: Kannada, English, and where the language question actually matters
body: Every Bangalore SEO pitch eventually offers you Kannada content. For a B2B software company, decline it.

Your buyer is an engineering or ops lead who reads documentation in English and searches in English. There is no meaningful Kannada query set for "API gateway pricing", and building one costs a quarter you can't get back.

Consumer and retail search is a different problem, and there the mix is real. Bangalore's customer base is genuinely multilingual — Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Hindi and Malayalam inside the same pin code — and much of that demand arrives as Romanised transliteration rather than Kannada script. Google treats the two as different query strings, and keyword tools under-report the script versions badly.
bullets: **For D2C and retail:** get the transliterated versions of your category and brand names into your Google Business Profile description, your product titles and your review replies — the places real customers' own words already appear.
**For B2B:** spend that budget on comparison pages instead. Your buyer isn't the constraint; your page inventory is.
**For everyone:** don't build a parallel Kannada site unless you can staff it permanently. A half-maintained language version is a duplicate-content problem wearing a growth hat.

sections.h2: Koramangala, HSR and Indiranagar: when the map pack is the whole game
body: If you sell software, skip this section. If you run stores, studios, clinics or a cloud kitchen, it's the only section that matters.

Google weights local results heavily by the searcher's distance from your pin, and Bangalore is spread out with traffic worse than the map suggests. Someone in Koramangala and someone in Whitefield see different three-packs for identical words. They're an hour apart.
bullets: **Koramangala, HSR Layout and Indiranagar sit close enough to bleed into each other.** One well-run listing can realistically pull all three. Whitefield, Yelahanka and Electronic City are not pulled in by anything short of a second physical address.
**Reviews are the fastest feedback loop in the entire channel.** Ask at the counter while the customer is still standing there, not by email three days later.
**Give every outlet its own page** with the real address, real hours and an embedded map. A single "Locations" page with five addresses on it ranks for none of them.

callout.title: Where the local work sits in a retainer
callout.body: Profile and review work is cheap in hours and disproportionate in return, which is why it comes first on every retail engagement. The full breakdown is on [our SEO service page](/seo).

sections.h2: What the 90-day guarantee means on a site under 500 pages
body: We freeze one number on day one: your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search, taken from your CRM rather than your analytics. Beat it in 90 days or we keep working free until we do. We never promise a position for a keyword — nobody controls Google's index.

The reason that promise is even survivable on a Bangalore startup site is page count. A 30-to-300-page product site has a small, knowable set of problems: a JavaScript rendering issue, a sitemap nobody has updated since the last replatform, twelve pages competing for the same query, and no bottom-funnel inventory at all. Those are 90-day problems.
It's also why we only take three clients a month. You cannot carry that risk at volume — the maths of it is the same maths that makes agencies with forty accounts quietly stop caring about yours.

callout.title: When we'll tell you the window is wrong
callout.body: If you're a marketplace with 50,000 URLs and a decade of redirect debt, 90 days is not enough time to beat your baseline and we will say so before we quote. Taking that engagement on those terms would just be a slower way of failing you.

sections.h2: Three ways Bangalore SEO usually goes wrong
body: We hear the same three post-mortems here, almost word for word.
numbered: **Publishing for other founders instead of buyers.** Bangalore rewards writing that does well on LinkedIn. That audience is your peers, not your pipeline. Both are worth having; only one belongs in the SEO budget.

**Treating docs as somebody else's problem.** For a developer-facing product the documentation subdomain often out-earns the blog, and it's usually unowned, unindexed and unmeasured. Check whether yours is even in Search Console.

**Buying traffic reporting instead of lead reporting.** If the monthly deck opens with sessions, you're being managed rather than served. Ask what the number was on day one and what it is now — the same place [what SEO costs in India](/cost/seo-cost-in-india) starts from.

faqs.q: How much does an SEO agency in Bangalore cost?
faqs.a: Advertised packages start around ₹10,000 a month and reach ₹3,00,000 for enterprise scope. Below roughly ₹25,000 you are funding part-time attention, not a team. We start at ₹75,000/mo, with smaller sites from ₹40,000, ex-GST, month-to-month after the first quarter.

faqs.q: Do I need Kannada content to rank in Bangalore?
faqs.a: For B2B software, no — your buyers search in English and there is no real Kannada query set for technical product terms. For D2C, retail and local services it matters, but mostly as Romanised transliteration in your Google Business Profile, product titles and reviews rather than as a full second-language site.

faqs.q: How long before a Bangalore startup sees results from SEO?
faqs.a: Impressions for target queries usually move inside 4–8 weeks. Bottom-funnel comparison and alternatives pages can rank in weeks because so few companies write them properly. Category head terms take two to four quarters and need links. Anyone quoting faster than that on a competitive term is quoting a different problem.

faqs.q: Is SEO or paid search better for a Bangalore SaaS company?
faqs.a: Paid gives you a knowable cost per lead from day one and never gets cheaper on its own. Organic costs more in year one and less in year two, because the pages keep working. Most funded companies here need both — the mistake is funding one from the other's budget mid-quarter.

faqs.q: Do you work with Bangalore companies selling outside India?
faqs.a: Yes, and it changes the technical brief rather than the strategy. You'll need hreflang set correctly, a link profile that isn't entirely Indian domains, and copy that matches how buyers in that market phrase the problem. We price the same way regardless of where the revenue lands.

faqs.q: What happens if you miss the 90-day target?
faqs.a: We keep working at no charge until we beat the frozen baseline. The baseline is your trailing-90-day qualified organic leads, pulled from your CRM on day one and agreed in writing before any work starts. We do not guarantee ranking positions, because nobody honest can.
